overview.text:
**Changed**
- `src/index.ts:parse`: when the single-value regex fails, it now scans the input with a sticky regex `part` (`/iy`) instead of returning `NaN` [E6, H3].
- Each component needs a number and a unit, and must be followed by a digit, `-`, `.`, or end of input. Otherwise the function returns `NaN` [H3].
- Each component is converted by calling `parse(component[0])` recursively and added to `total`. The result is returned only if `count > 1` [H3].
- Sign rule: the first component's sign is stored in `sign`. A later component with a different sign returns `NaN`. There is no `+` in the regex, so `1h +30m` fails [H3].
- Spaces between components are skipped. A trailing space returns `NaN`. Tabs and commas also fail [H3, H2].
- `README.md`: added `parse('1h 30m')` and `parse('2d3h')` examples and a paragraph on compound syntax, the sign rule, the 100-character limit, and the `StringValue` limitation [E7, H1].

**Why**
- The user wanted compound durations summed in milliseconds, single-unit inputs unchanged, `NaN` for mixed signs or invalid parts, and the 100-character limit kept [E1].
- The agent kept the existing single-unit path "intact" and added "a full-string compound check that requires a unit on every part and consistent signs" [E5].
- The comment in `H3` says the single-value parser stays "the source of unit conversions", which is why it recurses [H3].

**Tests**
- New file `src/compound.test.ts` with three `node:test` cases [E7, H2]:
  - Sums: `1h 30m`, `2d3h`, `1 hour 30 minutes`, `1.5h 10s`, `1mo 2ms .5S`, `-1h -30m`, each with an exact millisecond value [H2].
  - Rejects: `1h -30m`, `-1h 30m`, `1h +30m`, `1h 30`, `1h 30x`, junk, a comma, leading or trailing space, and a tab. Each must be `NaN` [H2].
  - Preserves: `100`, `-.5 hr`, `1   MiNuTe`, and a 100-character string all parse. A 101-character string and `''` throw. `1s ` gives `NaN` [H2].
- `node --test src/compound.test.ts` exited 0. The agent reports all three passed; the pass lines are truncated in the output [E8, E9].
- `tsc --noEmit` was skipped because TypeScript is not installed. `git diff --check` was clean [E8].

**Risks**
- The existing suites (`parse.test.ts`, `parse-strict.test.ts`, `index.test.ts`, `format.test.ts`) were not run, so a regression in single-unit behaviour is not ruled out [E3, E8].
- Type checking was never done [E8, E9].
- The unit list is duplicated in the `part` regex, separate from the single-value regex. The two could drift apart [H3].
- The `ms` and `parseStrict` types (`StringValue`) were not extended. Only the README notes this [H1].
- The 100-character limit relies on an existing check outside this hunk. The tests exercise it, but the code is not shown [H2, H3].
- An initial `rg` on `MEMORY.md` exited 1, which was harmless [E3].

4. Edit `src/index.ts`: when the single-unit match fails, the old `return NaN` is replaced by a sticky regex loop [E6, H3]:
   - It matches each `number unit` part and recursively calls `parse(component[0])` to sum the parts [E6, H3].
   - It returns `NaN` on a sign mismatch, an unmatched part, or trailing space [E6, H3].

   - Single-value behaviour and the 100-character limit: 99 characters parse, 100 throw [E7, H2].
6. Edit README: added `1h 30m` and `2d3h` examples and a paragraph on the compound rules [E7, H1]. The paragraph covers sign rules, the 100-character limit, and the fact that `StringValue` only covers single values [E7, H1].

11. Report: summarised the compound support, README changes, no installed dependencies, and that type checking was not run [E9].

13. Not verified: TypeScript type correctness of the new code [E8].

mechanism.text:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["parse(str)"] --> B["existing single-value regex match"]
  B -->|"match.groups present"| C["existing single-unit conversion (unchanged)"]
  B -->|"no match"| D["compound loop: offset = 0, sign undefined, total = 0, count = 0"]
  D -->|"offset < str.length"| E["sticky regex part.exec(str) at offset"]
  E -->|"null"| N["return NaN"]
  E -->|"component found"| F["negative = component[1] starts with '-'"]
  F -->|"sign set and differs"| N
  F -->|"sign consistent"| G["total += parse(component[0]); count++"]
  G -->|"recursive call on one component"| C
  G --> H["offset = lastIndex; skip spaces"]
  H -->|"at end and str ends with ' '"| N
  H -->|"more input"| E
  H -->|"offset == length"| I["count > 1 ?"]
  I -->|"yes"| J["return total (ms)"]
  I -->|"no"| N
```
Flow above is derived from the final `src/index.ts` change [H3].

- **Entry and fallback.** The compound logic only runs when the existing single-value regex fails, where the old code did `return NaN`. Single-unit inputs that matched before still take the unchanged path [H3].
- **Sticky component regex `part` (`/iy`).** It is used for each component [H3].
  - It matches `-?\d*\.?\d+`, optional spaces, then a unit alternation [H3].
  - A lookahead requires the next thing to be ` *-?\d`, ` *-?\.\d`, or end of string [H3].
  - The sticky flag anchors each match at `offset`, so gaps or junk cause `exec` to return null and the function returns `NaN` [H3].
- **Sign check.** `sign` records whether the first component is negative. Any later component with a different sign returns `NaN`, so `-1h -30m` passes and `1h -30m` / `-1h 30m` fail [H3, H2].
- **Unit conversion.** Each matched component string (e.g. `30m`) goes back into `parse` recursively. The single-value path stays the only source of conversion factors, and results are summed into `total` [H3].
- **Advance.** `offset` moves to `lastIndex` and then past any spaces. A trailing-space guard (`offset === str.length && str.endsWith(' ')`) returns `NaN`. From reading the regex, the lookahead likely rejects trailing spaces before this guard runs; that is not verified [H3].
- **`count > 1` gate.** A lone component that reached the fallback (e.g. `1s `) can never be accepted through the compound path [H3].
- **Accept tests** run through the loop and `count > 1`: `1h 30m`, `2d3h`, `1 hour 30 minutes`, `1.5h 10s`, `1mo 2ms .5S`, `-1h -30m` [H2, H3].
- **Reject tests** hit these exits [H2, H3]:
  - Null `exec`: `1h 30`, `1h 30x`, `1h 30m junk`, `1h,30m`, `1h\t30m`, `1h +30m`, and leading-space ` 1h 30m` [H2, H3].
  - Sign mismatch: `1h -30m`, `-1h 30m` [H2].
- **Single-value tests** (`100`, `-.5 hr`, `1   MiNuTe`) exercise the unchanged branch [H2, H3].
  - The 100-character throw and the `''` throw are asserted in tests; the code producing them is pre-existing and not shown in the hunk [H2, H3].
  - `1s ` returns `NaN` via the compound path [H2, H3].
- **Verification.** One test run and one type-check attempt are shown [E8].
  - `node --test src/compound.test.ts` exited 0, and the agent reports 3 tests passed. The full test output is truncated in the evidence [E8, E9].
  - `tsc` was not run because TypeScript is not installed [E8].
  - The existing test files `src/parse.test.ts` and `src/index.test.ts` were not run [E3, E8].
